card: - Causal: The sentence contains cause-effect meaning. The label follows the PDTB-3 definition for CONTINGENCY: "one argument provides the reason, explanation or justification for the situation described by the other." It covers four senses: CAUSE: Arg1 and Arg2 are causally influenced but not in a conditional relation (example connectives "because", "since"); PURPOSE: One Arg describes the goal while the other Arg describes the action undertaken to achieve the goal ("in order to", "so that"); CONDITION: One Arg presents an unrealized situation, that when realized, would lead to the situation described by the other Arg ("if", "as long as"); NEGATIVE-CONDITION: One Arg presents an unrealized situation, that if it does not occur, would lead to the situation described by the other Arg ("till", "unless"). Senses that provide reasons for the speaker to utter a speech, or the hearer to have a belief, are not annotated as causal.
label_definitions_source: official: CNC annotation manual 'Event Causality in Socio-Political News - Annotation Manual' (https://github.com/tanfiona/CausalNewsCorpus/blob/4796c7e89d9b346f8e1280dac441dacde2be6b86/documentation/Event_Causality_Manual_for_CASE_2022_Public.pdf), section 3.1.1 General Definition (PDTB-3 CONTINGENCY and its CAUSE / PURPOSE / CONDITION / NEGATIVE-CONDITION senses) and the +SPEECH-ACT/+BELIEF exclusion; quoted near-verbatim (the CONTINGENCY definition and the four sense definitions are verbatim; the 'Example connectives are X and Y' sentences are condensed into parentheses and the exclusion sentence is lightly shortened), with a short lead-in sentence paraphrasing the Subtask 1 description ('identifies if a given event sentence contains any cause-effect meaning').
source: Causal News Corpus V2, official GitHub repo (not the HF conversion)
citation: Tan et al. (2022), The Causal News Corpus: Annotating Causal Relations in Event Sentences from News, LREC 2022 (documentation/2022.lrec-1.246.pdf in the repo); Tan et al. (2022), Event Causality Identification with Causal News Corpus - Shared Task 3, CASE@EMNLP 2022.

text_date_range: unknown per item; sentences come from English socio-political news (China and South Africa sources) reused from the CASE 2021 Subtask 4 corpus; corpus published 2022 (V1) / V2 files last changed 2023-05-10
sampling: per class: dev rows sorted by index, random.Random(20261026).shuffle, take first 72; rows then shuffled with the same RNG
state_format: sentence text verbatim from the CSV 'text' column (leading/trailing whitespace stripped only)
uncertain: Track U: CNC dev is public since 2022 (V1) / 2023 (V2) and CNC train/dev are widely used for training, so contamination is possible; dev gold labels are public.
All index values in dev_subtask1.csv start with 'train_' (inherited from the CASE 2021 source corpus ids); this is the source's own naming, and the file used is dev_subtask1.csv at the pinned commit.
Text is pre-tokenised news sentences (spaces before punctuation) and a few contain page boilerplate such as 'PUBLISHED : <date>'; kept verbatim because the label applies to the whole annotated text.

The card's first sentence is a close paraphrase of the manual's Subtask 1 description; the sense definitions are verbatim, connective examples and the +SPEECH-ACT/+BELIEF exclusion are lightly condensed.
